happy.definition: Feeling or showing pleasure, contentment, and joy.
happy.exampleUsage: The children were very happy to visit their grandparents on Eid.

joyful.definition: Feeling, expressing, or causing great happiness and delight.
joyful.exampleUsage: A joyful atmosphere filled the house when the newborn arrived.

excited.definition: Feeling eager and enthusiastic about something that is going to happen.
excited.exampleUsage: The students are excited about tomorrow's science trip.

proud.definition: Feeling pleased and satisfied about an achievement or good work.
proud.exampleUsage: His parents were proud when he graduated from university.

grateful.definition: Feeling or showing sincere appreciation and thankfulness.
grateful.exampleUsage: We are deeply grateful for our good health and supportive family.

content.definition: In a state of peaceful satisfaction with what one has.
content.exampleUsage: He felt calm and content after finishing his daily tasks.

amused.definition: Finding something funny or entertaining, often shown with a smile.
amused.exampleUsage: Everyone at the table was amused by the grandfather's clever story.

delighted.definition: Feeling or showing great pleasure and satisfaction.
delighted.exampleUsage: She was delighted to receive a handwritten letter from her sister.

cheerful.definition: Noticeably happy, bright, and optimistic in manner.
cheerful.exampleUsage: The shopkeeper greets every customer with a cheerful smile.

hopeful.definition: Feeling optimistic and confident that good things will happen in the future.
hopeful.exampleUsage: The farmers remain hopeful that rain will fall this week.

sad.definition: Feeling unhappy or sorrowful, often because of a loss or disappointment.
sad.exampleUsage: He felt sad when his best friend moved to another city.

angry.definition: Feeling strong displeasure about something unfair or upsetting.
angry.exampleUsage: Take a deep breath and speak calmly when you feel angry.

scared.definition: Feeling afraid, fearful, or nervous about a possible danger.
scared.exampleUsage: The little cat was scared of the loud thunder outside.

worried.definition: Feeling uneasy or troubled about a problem or something that might happen.
worried.exampleUsage: Parents naturally feel worried when a child has a fever.

frustrated.definition: Feeling annoyed or discouraged because you cannot achieve or fix something.
frustrated.exampleUsage: He felt frustrated when the computer froze before he saved his work.

disappointed.definition: Feeling sad because something did not turn out as well as hoped.
disappointed.exampleUsage: The team was disappointed after losing the final match.

upset.definition: Feeling unhappy, distressed, or emotionally troubled by an event.
upset.exampleUsage: She was upset when her favorite teacup broke on the tile floor.

annoyed.definition: Feeling slightly angry or impatient because of an irritation.
annoyed.exampleUsage: The neighbors were annoyed by the loud construction noise outside.

bored.definition: Feeling tired and restless because you have nothing interesting to do.
bored.exampleUsage: The passengers grew bored during the three-hour delay at the station.

lonely.definition: Feeling sad because you are alone and miss the company of others.
lonely.exampleUsage: During his first week abroad, the student felt a little lonely.

calm.definition: Peaceful, quiet, and free from anger, nervousness, or strong worry.
calm.exampleUsage: The pilot spoke in a calm voice to reassure the passengers.

tired.definition: Needing rest or sleep after working hard or staying awake for a long time.
tired.exampleUsage: After painting the living room all day, we were too tired to cook.

surprised.definition: Feeling sudden wonder or amazement because something unexpected happened.
surprised.exampleUsage: He was pleasantly surprised to see his uncle waiting at the airport.

confused.definition: Unable to understand something clearly or unsure of what to do.
confused.exampleUsage: The visitor looked confused by the train station map, so I offered help.

curious.definition: Eager to ask questions, explore, and learn how things work.
curious.exampleUsage: The curious student asked the teacher how eclipses happen.

thoughtful.definition: Quietly absorbed in thinking, or showing kind consideration for others.
thoughtful.exampleUsage: It was very thoughtful of you to bring hot soup to our sick neighbor.

relaxed.definition: Feeling comfortable, rested, and free from tension or worry.
relaxed.exampleUsage: Everyone felt relaxed while sitting in the shaded courtyard.

indifferent.definition: Having no particular interest, concern, or preference one way or the other.
indifferent.exampleUsage: He was indifferent about whether we ate rice or pasta for dinner.

sleepy.definition: Feeling drowsy and ready to fall asleep.
sleepy.exampleUsage: The warm room made the children sleepy after lunch.

alert.definition: Fully awake, attentive, and quick to notice what is happening around you.
alert.exampleUsage: A good driver stays alert and watches the road carefully.

hungry.definition: Feeling the need or desire to eat food.
hungry.exampleUsage: After a morning of hiking in the hills, everyone was hungry.

thirsty.definition: Feeling dry in the mouth and needing to drink water.
thirsty.exampleUsage: Working outdoors under the summer sun made the gardeners very thirsty.

full.definition: Satisfied after eating enough food and not needing any more.
full.exampleUsage: Thank you for the delicious dinner, I am completely full.

cold.definition: Feeling uncomfortably chilly and needing warm clothes or a blanket.
cold.exampleUsage: Put on your wool coat so you do not feel cold outside.

hot.definition: Having a high body temperature or feeling uncomfortably warm.
hot.exampleUsage: We sat under the shade of the palm trees because the afternoon was hot.

dizzy.definition: Feeling unsteady and lightheaded, as if the room is spinning around you.
dizzy.exampleUsage: Stand up slowly if you feel dizzy after bending down.

nauseous.definition: Feeling sick in the stomach, as if you might vomit.
nauseous.exampleUsage: Reading in a moving car on a winding road makes him feel nauseous.

exhausted.definition: Completely drained of energy and extremely tired.
exhausted.exampleUsage: The rescue workers were exhausted after working through the night.

energetic.definition: Full of lively physical and mental energy.
energetic.exampleUsage: A good night's sleep leaves you feeling fresh and energetic.

comfortable.definition: Feeling physically at ease and free from pain, discomfort, or stress.
comfortable.exampleUsage: Make sure your chair is at a comfortable height before studying.
